verdicts.quote: one user is created per row, all or none: after the request, either every row's user exists or none does.
Each entry has `row` (1-based data row, or null for file/header errors), `column` (or null), a stable machine-readable `code`, and a human-readable `message`.

If an email already belongs to an existing user, that row is an error `EMAIL_EXISTS`... If the same email appears more than once in the file, the first occurrence is kept and every later occurrence is an error

otherwise must be a role the uploader is allowed to assign (`ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED`...)... a role the uploader may not assign ... → `ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED`, nothing created (no privilege escalation through CSV).
the bulk-import operation is available only to an authenticated user who currently holds the admin role.
verdicts.missing: Whether bulk import is a distinct permission from single-user creation; the spec ties it to the admin role (definition open in G-4) and never says that being able to create one user does not grant import.

verdicts.quote: the header must contain `email` (required)... Unknown columns, or a duplicated column, reject the whole file... Each row must have exactly as many fields as the header (`ROW_FIELD_COUNT`).
optional double-quote quoting with `""` escapes (quoted fields may contain commas and line breaks), LF or CRLF line endings, UTF-8 encoding with an optional leading BOM (stripped).
any failure before commit leaves the store unchanged; failure during commit rolls back everything (or compensates, G-6)
A body larger than `MAX_BYTES` is rejected `FILE_TOO_LARGE` (HTTP 413)... more than `MAX_ROWS` data rows is rejected `TOO_MANY_ROWS` (422).
verdicts.missing: The actual values of MAX_BYTES and MAX_ROWS are left open (G-1).

verdicts.quote: is zero bytes, or has a header but no data rows is rejected as a whole with a file-level error (... `EMPTY_FILE`, `NO_DATA_ROWS`)
A second submission of an already imported file is not an error of the system: every row is `EMAIL_EXISTS` (R-4), nothing changes.
parse, validate and write within the upload request; the outcome is in the response. No job queue, background worker, status endpoint or notification.
verdicts.missing: Whether a maximum-size file actually fits in a synchronous request is unresolved (G-1); the background alternative is deferred, not decided.

verdicts.quote: The feature sends no email or other notification (A-7).
Created users are put in the same initial state a single-created user would be (G-2). The feature creates no usable credential on its own.
verdicts.missing: Active vs pending and how a bulk-created user first signs in are left open (G-2).

verdicts.quote: held only for the duration of the request, in memory (or request-scoped temporary storage deleted at request end, success or failure)... not retained afterwards.
locale-delimited (semicolon) files are rejected with an explanatory header error.
verdicts.missing: How the values themselves are handled across locales (Unicode normalisation of names, any date/number formats) is not stated; only the delimiter is addressed.

verdicts.quote: one record per attempt, written for success and for rejection: timestamp, uploader id, outcome (`created`, `rejected`, `conflict`, `failed`), row count, created count
recovery is to look at the user list or resubmit — the resubmission result (`EMAIL_EXISTS` rows) shows what was created. There is no automatic retry and no import identifier.
verdicts.missing: Cancelling a running import is not addressed at all; retrying only failed rows is implied away by atomicity but not stated.

verdicts.quote: at `MAX_ROWS` rows the request completes within the runtime's request time limit (value from G-1, **unresolved**).
verdicts.missing: The time bound has no value; progress is only an indeterminate status (R-11), not progress through the rows.

verdicts.quote: existing users are never modified or overwritten.
verdicts.missing: Nothing says the existing single-user creation path stays unchanged and keeps working; the spec only reuses its rules.

verdicts.quote: no CSV, XLSX or other export is produced by this feature, so spreadsheet-formula injection on output does not apply
